questions.text: The set of attributes X will be fully functionally dependent on the set of attributes Y if the following conditions are satisfied.
questions.solution:
X is fully functionally dependent on Y when [latex]Y\rightarrow X[/latex] holds and no proper subset of Y determines X. Both conditions are needed.

Answer: Both (A) and (B)

options: X is functionally dependent on Y
X is not functionally dependent on any subset of Y

questions.text: Immunity of the external schemas (or application programs) to changes in the conceptual scheme is referred to as:
questions.solution:
Being able to change the conceptual (logical) schema without changing external schemas or applications is logical data independence. Physical independence is about the internal (storage) schema.

Answer: Logical Data Independence

questions.text: In E-R model, Y is the dominant entity and X is subordinate entity
questions.solution:
The subordinate (weak) entity X depends on the dominant entity Y for its existence. Deleting Y must delete its dependent X entities.

Answer: If Y is deleted, then X is also deleted

If Y is deleted, then X is also deleted
If Y is deleted, then X is not deleted

questions.text: Which of the following is dense index?
questions.solution:
A secondary index is on a non-ordering field, so it must have an entry for every record: a dense index. Primary and clustered indexes can be sparse (one entry per block or per value).

Answer: Secondary index

questions.text: in a file which contains 1 million records and the order of the tree is 100, then what is the maximum number of nodes to be accessed if B+ tree index is used?
questions.solution:
In the worst case nodes are only half full, so each node has about 50 children. [latex]50^3=125{,}000 \lt 10^6\le50^4[/latex], so the tree needs 4 levels: 4 node accesses.

Answer: 4
